title: fix(plugin-approvals): an approval's status write-back runs its automation as the person who acted, in the record's organisation
body:
Fixes #24519
Clause-②: no (a producer fix inside `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`: no `@objectstack/spec` key, export, type or stored column moves; ruled by `6271152775`)

The status write-back an approval makes (`approvalStatusField`) now runs the automation it fires as the person who acted, with that person's own request envelope in the record's organisation. Ruling `6271152775` on #24519 (maintainer: Gap 1 「A 带记录组织」, the cross-organisation approver 「x 按记录组织」, the live widening 「随 #24519 一起修」).

**Landing order.** The claim made this PR wait for PR #24527 (#24321), which edits the same file at the decision to resume hand-off. PR #24527 has merged (`1b4078077`), and this branch merges `origin/main` past it at `8b118b6b3`. The two changes touch disjoint regions. The PR stays draft for the seat's review of record.

## What was wrong

`ApprovalService.mirrorStatusField` wrote as `{ isSystem: true, userId, positions: [], permissions: [] }`, with no organisation, on every door that names a person: submit (through the approval node), approve, reject, recall, send back (returned and auto-reject), and the action link. Phase 1 (report `6270420946`) measured on a real stack what a `runAs: 'user'` consumer of that write received:
- a `runAs: 'user'` hook kept the carried empty arrays verbatim (the rule PR #24518 keeps for a narrowed ceiling), so it ran on the member baseline instead of the person's own grants, and it saw only the person in `sys_user`;
- a `runAs: 'user'` record-change flow fired by the write got no organisation, so its grants resolved organisation-less, which is not the person's request in the record's organisation.

The docblock's reason for leaving the organisation off no longer held: since #10101 the request's organisation is the subject record's, and under `single` the driver scopes nothing. Its other claim, that the automation engine back-fills the run's `tenantId`, was false: the grants bridge answers a `tenantId` only when it was handed one.

## The change

- **`mirrorStatusField`'s named-actor branch** writes under `attributedMirrorContext(...)`: `{ isSystem: true, userId, tenantId }` and nothing else.
  - `tenantId` is the subject record's LIVE organisation. It is read at write time, one by-id read of the organisation column, through `recordOrgResolver`, the resolver the request row was stamped by. The request's organisation is the fallback for an object (or a record) with none, as at the stamp.
  - No `positions` / `permissions`. The write itself is authorized by `isSystem` alone (the security middleware short-circuits before it reads a grant), so it still crosses the record lock and still lands a read-only status column. Every `runAs: 'user'` consumer now resolves the person's own envelope in that organisation.
- **The user-less branch** (the dead-run sweep) keeps `SYSTEM_CTX`: a `runAs: 'user'` automation it fires is still refused.
- **Every attributed write acts in the record's organisation,** an approver drawn from another organisation's directory (ADR-0105 D9) included. That is the reading PR #24527 applies to a `runAs: 'user'` decider.
- **The six call sites** each pass the request organisation they already hold (`org` / `requestOrg`) as the fallback: one argument each.
- **The docblock** is rewritten, the false back-fill sentence included.
- **Untouched**, as the claim fences: `approval-node.ts`, `SYSTEM_CTX`, the action-link context (Phase 1 measured that no write is made under any of them), and PR #24527's resume hand-off.

## Pins

`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/status-mirror-envelope.integration.test.ts` (new, 10 cases). It uses a real kernel, the real ObjectQL engine and hook wrappers, the real record-change trigger and automation engine, the real `ApprovalService` and approval node executor, and driver-sql on better-sqlite3 `:memory:`. The authz tables the resolver reads are spelled locally (the `status-mirror-cascade` precedent: no new dependency, no lockfile change), and the security catalog is bound with the package's test kit. The fixture is synthetic: two organisations; a person whose memberships differ between them; a person holding a grant the baseline lacks; an approver from the other organisation.

For each door that names a person, the envelope a `runAs: 'user'` hook and a `runAs: 'user'` record-change flow receive equals `resolveUserAuthzGrants(person, { tenantId: ORG })` (positions, permission sets, peers), and the write carries `isSystem`, the person, `ORG` and no arrays:
- open through the approval node (the submitter), approve, reject, recall, send back, send back past the revision limit, action-link redeem;
- direction 1: the grant held beyond the baseline is carried (approve, reject);
- direction 2: the person whose memberships differ carries only the record organisation's (open, recall);
- the approver from another organisation acts in the record's organisation, with its members as peers;
- a record re-parented while its request was pending is written, and cascades, in its new organisation;
- CONTROL: the dead-run sweep stays user-less, the hook is refused (`HOOK_UNSCOPED_DATA_ACCESS`), and the flow runs with no person.

What the security plugin then enforces for an envelope stays pinned where the seed lives (`service-automation`'s `runas-user-hook-org-peers.integration.test.ts`).

**Moved pin, one:** `approval-service.test.ts` › `status mirror identity (#3783)` asserted the mirror carries NO `tenantId`, which is the contract the ruling reverses. It now asserts the full context, `{ isSystem: true, userId: 'u1', tenantId: 't1' }`, on that suite's schema-less engine double (the request's organisation as the fallback). The other nine pins of that describe are unchanged and green. Kin sweep: no other package test reaches the real mirror.

## Ablation (fix committed first; `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on `approval-service.ts`; the suite imports the service from source, so no dist leg)

Both legs were predicted before running: 9 red (every door that names a person), the CONTROL green.
- **Leg 1, restore the empty arrays** (`{ ...SYSTEM_CTX, userId, tenantId }`; blob `9ceb29f2c7f9` → `d2258164b9de`): **9 failed / 1 passed**. Each fails at the hook's envelope: positions and permission sets `[]` where the person's own were expected.
- **Leg 2, drop the organisation** (`{ isSystem: true, userId }`; blob `9ceb29f2c7f9` → `3522d1ac69f9`): **9 failed / 1 passed**. Each fails at the hook's envelope: `tenantId` undefined, peers = the person alone, and positions and permission sets that are not the record organisation's.
- Each leg restored by the tool: blob after restore `9ceb29f2c7f9` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Tests and gates (final head `8b118b6b3`, which merges `origin/main` at `65a8eeb7d`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test`: 83 files, 1132 tests passed (`TEST_EXIT=0`, under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0; `check:test-typecheck: OK` (324 errors / 27 signatures held, debt unchanged).
- Derived gates (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, no paths, after the last commit): 69 commands, all 69 exit 0. `--ran`: `69 derived, 69 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
  - On the first pass, `check:query-options-erasure` and `check:slot-lookup` each flagged one new erasure in this diff. Both were fixed by typing (the record read no longer casts its options; the pin's engine lookup is typed `ObjectQL`), not by baselining.
  - `check:i18n` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`); after a full `turbo run build` both exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs`: OK.
- CI's families are read from this PR's check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **Same family, out of this PR:** `service-automation`'s `resolveRunDataContext` system arm carries `positions: []` / `permissions: []` beside a carried `userId`. It is the shape PR #24527's `runAs: 'system'` post-decision segment writes with. The seat files it as its own family card under the same rule (ruling `6271152775` item 5).
- **Visible to hook authors:** on a mirror write, `ctx.session.organizationId` now carries the organisation, and `ctx.session.positions` is absent instead of `[]`. The changeset says so.
- **Cost:** one by-id read of the record's organisation column per named-actor mirror write, skipped for an object with no organisation column.
- **Walled posture:** naming the record's live organisation scopes the mirror update to that organisation (and organisation-less rows), which the record always satisfies. A `runAs: 'system'` cascade of the mirror is now org-scoped there as well, the #5494 posture user-triggered system runs already have.
